Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Nova Renewables Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. As a further reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Nova Renewables Inc.'s results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Development Officer; Liam O'Connor, Chief Technology Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Sustainability Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Operating Officer; Emma Larsson, Chief Strategy Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Nova Renewables continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in Q2. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Today, I want to highlight eight key aspects of our performance:

1. Capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets. Good afternoon, everyone. I'm thrilled with our execution so far this year, and as we pivot to our forward guidance, let me dive into our capacity addition outlook and project pipeline targets. This is the engine driving our growth story in the clean tech space, fueled by unprecedented policy tailwinds, plummeting hardware costs, and our differentiated development platform.

To recap, in FY2023, we delivered a record 2.8 GW of new capacity additions across our core segments: utility-scale solar PV at 1.9 GW, onshore wind at 600 MW, and battery energy storage systems—or BESS—at 300 MWh co-located with our solar projects. This represented a 45% year-over-year increase, with an average blended capacity factor of 28% post-optimization, thanks to our proprietary AI-driven yield management software that boosted energy yield by 5-7% on average.

Looking ahead, our FY2024 capacity addition guidance is set at 3.2 to 3.6 GW, implying 15-30% growth over last year. For FY2025, we're raising the bar to 4.8 to 5.4 GW, positioning us for over 90% cumulative growth from FY2023 levels by FY2026. These targets are conservative relative to our pipeline strength—we're not baking in any late-cycle upside from emerging markets like green hydrogen electrolyzers, which we're piloting at 50 MW scale. Breaking it down by technology:

Utility-scale solar PV: 2.4-2.7 GW in FY2024, which is 75% of total, ramping to 3.6-4.0 GW in FY2025. We're shifting toward high-efficiency n-type TOPCon modules with 22.5%+ efficiencies, sourced from our strategic offtake with JinkoSolar and LONGi. Bifacial ratios are hitting 80% on new builds, delivering 10-15% more kWh per MWdc versus legacy PERC tech.

Onshore wind: 500-700 MW annually through FY2025. We're focusing on IEC Class III turbines from Vestas' EN147 series, optimized for low-wind regimes in the US Midwest and India. Hybrid wind-solar farms, like our 300 MW Michigan project, are key, with integrated BESS unlocking 40% higher revenue capture via arbitrage and ancillary services.

BESS and hybrids: 500-700 MWh in FY2024, scaling to 1.2 GW / 2.4 GWh by FY2025. Drawing from Tesla Megapack economics—now at sub-$150/kWh system cost—we're deploying 4-hour duration systems co-located with 70% of our solar additions. This de-risks intermittency and supports ERCOT and CAISO frequency regulation markets, where we've secured 15-year contracts at $25-30/kW-month fixed.

Regionally, the US remains our powerhouse, accounting for 65% of FY2024 additions and 55% of FY2025. The Inflation Reduction Act—or IRA—continues to supercharge us: our effective ITC yield is now 45-50% with adders for domestic content—85% US-made modules via our Nevada factory ramp—and energy communities. Texas and the Southwest dominate, with 1.2 GW CODs slated for H2 2024 in ERCOT, backed by 12 GWh of merchant exposure hedged via virtual PPAs with Amazon and Microsoft. California PPAs are locked at $35-40/MWh, competitive with gas peakers post-LCOE convergence.

Europe contributes 20% of our guidance, laser-focused on Spain and Italy under REPowerEU's 320 GW solar target by 2030. We've got 400 MW shovel-ready in Andalusia, leveraging EU CBAM tariffs that penalize Chinese imports—our European Content module sourcing hits 60%. Permitting headwinds persist, but our JV with Iberdrola has accelerated grid queue times to under 18 months.

Emerging markets round out at 15%: India—200 MW Rajasthan solar via SECI auctions at INR 2.5/kWh or ~$30/MWh—and Australia—150 MW Queensland wind-solar hybrid. These yield higher IRRs—18-22% versus 12-15% in OECD—at the expense of FX volatility, which we're mitigating with 80% USD-denominated PPAs.

Now, turning to our project pipeline targets, this is where our optionality shines. As of Q2 2024, our global development pipeline stands at 28.5 GW across 150+ projects—a 25% increase QoQ and 120% from two years ago. We've tiered it rigorously: Contracted / ITC-allocated totals 5.2 GW—70% solar, 15% wind, 1.1 GWh BESS—with 90% PPAs signed and $4.2B revenue backlog at avg $0.8M/MW EPC, CODs through 2027. Advanced development, shovel-ready, is 8.1 GW—65% solar, 20% wind, 1.8 GWh BESS—with PPAs in negotiation and 70% with investment-grade off-takers like Google and utilities; US queue positions top 10%. Early-stage is 15.2 GW—80% solar, 10% wind, 2.0 GWh BESS—with greenfield sites secured and brownfield repowers adding 2 GW wind. AI site selection is yielding 15% faster progression.

Strategically, we're prioritizing data center adjacency—20 GW of our pipeline is within 50 miles of hyperscaler campuses, tapping into the AI boom's 100 GW+ US demand by 2030 per EIA forecasts. Our C&I segment is growing 50% YoY to 800 MW by FY2025, with rooftop solar + storage for Walmart and Sysco at sub-10-year paybacks.

Technical initiatives are accelerating conversion rates: Our digital twin platform, licensed from DNV, has cut modeling errors by 8%, while drone-enabled O&M targets 99.2% availability. On storage, we're testing iron-air long-duration tech with Form Energy for 100-hour dispatch, first 10 MW pilot in 2025.

Supply chain resilience is baked in—90% locked for 2025 trackers from Nextracker and inverters from Sungrow, polysilicon hedged below $10/kg amid Red Sea disruptions. Capex guidance holds at $1.1-1.2M/MW solar, $1.5M/MW wind, reflecting 15% YoY cost deflation.

Risks remain: US interconnection queues average 4-5 years, though FERC Order 2023 reforms should shave 20-30%. Interest rates at 5%+ pressure levered IRRs, but our 60/40 equity-debt mix and green bond issuances keep WACC at 6.2%. Geopolitics could spike module prices 10-15%, but multi-supplier strategy derisks that.

In summary, our capacity guidance and pipeline position Nova Renewables to capture 2-3% US market share by 2027, with ROIC expanding to 12-14%. We're engineering the grid of tomorrow.

2. Overall performance highlights and key achievements. Good afternoon, everyone. I'm thrilled to discuss our overall performance highlights and key achievements, which underscore another quarter of exceptional execution amid a rapidly evolving clean tech landscape. As a leader in integrated solar-plus-storage solutions and next-gen electrolyzers for green hydrogen, we've exceeded financial targets and advanced strategic positioning propelled by the IRA, EU's Net-Zero Industry Act, and surging demand for dispatchable renewables.

Q2 revenue reached $428 million, a 52% year-over-year increase and 18% sequential growth. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY growth, driven by a 65% surge in ESS to $185 million from NexusFlow vanadium redox flow batteries—over 1.2 GWh managed globally. Solar PV contributed $210 million, up 42% YoY with TOPCon at 24.8% efficiency. Green Hydrogen added $33 million from electrolyzer shipments to Europe.

Adjusted EBITDA was $112 million at 26.2% margin, expanding 410 bps YoY, from Terawatt Valley facility ramping perovskite tandem cells to 500 MW, LCOE under $35/MWh. GAAP net income $68 million, or $0.72/share, beating guidance 15%.

We commissioned 850 MW solar-plus-storage, TTM 2.8 GW ahead of 3 GW FY24 target. Backlog $4.2 billion, up 38% YoY, $1.8 billion contracted ESS. Pipeline 12 GW, including 500 MW/2 GWh California hybrid.

North America 68% revenue, 72% growth on $750 million IRA PTC/ITC. Europe up 110% to $95 million on IPCEI Hy2Tech electrolyzer contracts. APAC 22%, 15% margins via US wafers.

Innovation: NexusFlow 2.0—12-hour flow battery, 90% RTE, zero degradation—powers 200 MWh ERCOT. R&D 9% revenue for DC fast-charging pilots. Emissions down 28% YoY, SBTi validated.

Tailwinds: 25% ESS CAGR, hydrogen 10x. US supply chain 85% domestic.

Q2 sets FY24 $1.9-2.0 billion revenue, 25%+ EBITDA.

3 through 8—strategic priorities, gross margin trends, debt levels, capital recycling, government incentives, and new PPAs—I'll turn to Michael to cover in detail alongside financials.

Now, I'll hand the call over to Michael Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Elena. Our financial performance in Q2 was exceptional. Revenue reached $1.25 billion, representing a 52% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $203 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $150 million, or $1.55 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue to $5.8-6.2 billion and earnings.

Let me expand on those key aspects Elena mentioned. Starting with gross margin and operating margin trends, which reflect structural tailwinds from falling input costs, efficiencies, and premium mix. Q2 gross margin was 28.5%, up 320 bps YoY from 25.2% and 110 bps sequentially. Drivers: polysilicon at $8.50/kg, down 60% from peaks, module COGS $0.24/W, down 15% QoQ. TOPCon and n-type HJT 65% of shipments, ASP $0.31/W. Vertical integration at Ohio Fab 3—80% utilization, IRA incentives, 1.2% efficiency gains, BOS down 8%. US margins 32% on 45% shipments, Europe 26%, APAC 27%.

Operating margins 12.3%, up 250 bps YoY, OpEx 16.2% of revenue. R&D $45 million for perovskites, SG&A efficient, BESS 18% margins. Q3 gross 29-30%, FY24 28.5-29%, operating 13-14%.

On debt levels and financing costs, total gross debt $5.2 billion, up from $4.9 billion YE23 on $750 million construction financing. Net debt $4.1 billion, net debt/EBITDA 3.2x, within 2.5-3.5x target. Blended interest 3.8%, down 70 bps: $1 billion green bonds at 3.2%, refinanced $600 million at SOFR+140 bps. Maturity 6.8 years, 75% fixed, coverage 5.2x. US IRA tax equity $450 million, WACC 5.2%. Capex 70% project debt, 30% tax equity.

Capital recycling through asset sales: Q3 $1.75 billion from 650 MW US solar to Brookfield/QIA at 8.2x multiple, 5.8% cap rate; 400 MW Europe wind+storage to BlackRock at 9.1x. YTD $4.2 billion, deleveraged to 2.8x, funded 1.4 GW. FY24 target $6-7 billion.

Impact of government incentives: 28% of EBITDA. IRA $245 million ITC/PTC/45X, EPC down 12% to $0.92/W. Europe REPowerEU €85 million. India SECI, Australia CIS. FY24 $1.1-1.3 billion.

New PPAs secured: 1.2 GW at avg $32/MWh LCOE net ITC, portfolio $34/MWh. 650 MW CAISO $38/MWh, 350 MW ERCOT $28/MWh, 200 MW PJM $30/MWh. FY24 3.4 GW, $33/MWh outlook.

Finally, strategic priorities and outlook: Q4 revenue $1.25-1.35 billion, EBITDA $425-475 million, 34-35% margins. FY25 revenue $5.8-6.2 billion, EBITDA $1.95-2.1 billion. Pillars: scale solar/storage $2.5 billion capex, offshore wind, digital/policy. US 65%, Europe 20%, emerging 15%.

I'll now turn the call over to Sarah Patel to discuss our project development activities.

Sarah Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, with 28.5 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring a substantial number of new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

Liam, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Liam O'Connor:
Thank you, Sarah. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing groundbreaking technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will revolutionize the energy landscape.

Next, Maria will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, Liam. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability.

Now, Raj will provide operational highlights.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Maria. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best-in-class practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing heavily in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to excel.

Emma, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Emma Larsson:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on executing our long-term strategic plan, which includes expanding our presence in key markets, diversifying our product offerings, and strengthening our partnerships. We are also actively exploring new opportunities in emerging areas such as green hydrogen and carbon capture.

And finally, Tom, can you address our risk management strategies?

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Emma. We have implemented robust risk management strategies to mitigate potential risks associated with our operations, including market risks, regulatory risks, and environmental risks. We are continuously monitoring and evaluating our risk profile and taking proactive steps to manage these risks effectively.

I'll turn it back to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all. In conclusion, Nova Renewables had a truly exceptional Q2. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our unwavering focus on sustainability will continue to drive long-term growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We'll pause for a moment to assemble the queue. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for investing in new technologies such as green hydrogen?

Liam O'Connor:
Thanks for the question, John. Green hydrogen is a key pillar of our long-term innovation roadmap, and we're actively investing through pilots and JVs. We're deploying 50 MW electrolyzers in FY24, scaling to 100 MW PEM stacks by 2025, leveraging US Hydrogen Hubs and EU IPCEI funding. Our Texas hub with Plug Power targets $450/kW CAPEX, down 18% on 45V PTCs, with 70 kW/kg output for wind-to-H2. This diversifies beyond solar/BESS, capturing 15% project margins amid IRENA's 10x capacity need by 2030. Capex allocation is 10-15% of R&D, integrated with Nexus AI for dispatch optimization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Lisa. Competition is intensifying, but our integrated model—25 GW pipeline, 85% domestic supply chain, AI yield uplift—sets us apart. We're outpacing peers via IRA domestic content for 50% ITC yields, data center adjacency for 20 GW, and recycling $4.2B YTD to fund high-IRR greenfield. Unlike pure developers, we retain minority stakes in sales for yield, targeting 12-14% ROIC. Merchant hedging and multi-region diversification—65% US, 20% Europe—mitigate price pressure, where our $33/MWh PPAs beat consensus.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

Tom Reilly:
Thanks, David. Climate change poses risks like extreme weather, but our strategies mitigate them effectively. We've modeled scenarios per TCFD, with drone O&M and digital twins ensuring 99.2% availability. BESS firming counters intermittency, insurance covers 95% of assets, and siting in low-risk zones like Southwest deserts minimizes exposure. Upside from policy—IRA energy communities—and carbon pricing in EU ETS. Sensitivity: 10% yield drop from events shaves 2% EBITDA, offset by diversification.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
What are your expectations for the long-term profitability of your renewable energy projects?

Michael Chen:
Rachel, long-term profitability remains strong, with levered IRRs 12-14% on new builds. Margins expanding to 34% on hybrids, recycling flywheel deleveraging to 2.8x, incentives $1.1B FY24. Portfolio yield 28% capacity factors, inflation-linked PPAs, low WACC 5.2%. FY25 FCF $1.2B funds growth, ROIC 12%+. Merchant tails and ancillary services add 20-40% uplift post-PPA.

Operator:
As a final reminder, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Nova Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
